# v3.26-dev

## Fixed

- **A long-standing misdiagnosis in the developer notes, and the wasted effort it kept causing.** Help text occasionally shipped with two words run together — "Click **View**on any row". The cause was recorded as an interaction between the build compiler and HTML entities such as `&mdash;`, with a warning that a local type-check would hide the problem.

  That was wrong on every point, and it sent two later reviews hunting for problems that did not exist. Testing all four combinations through the build compiler *and* the type-checker shows they agree exactly, and that entities make no difference at all: the only thing that matters is whether a **line break** falls between the word and the tag before it. This is ordinary, documented behaviour — and the original diagnosis, from the release that first fixed 34 of these, was right all along.

  No help text needed changing: the five places previously flagged were false alarms, and every genuine instance had already been fixed.

## Added

- **A build check for the real problem.** `npm run check:jsx` (also part of CI) flags any line break that would swallow a space and glue two words together in the interface. It found none, which is the point — it locks in a class of bug that is invisible to the editor, to linting and to the type-checker, and that reaches users as garbled wording in the help pages.
